correctness.rationale: For 1<p<=2 let q=p/(p-1), A=||kappa x+tau y||p, B=||kappa x-tau y||p. The standard Clarkson conjugate-exponent inequality yields A^q+B^q<=2(kappa^p+tau^p)^(q/p); AM-GM then yields sqrt(A B)<=(kappa^p+tau^p)^(1/p). Unit vectors on disjoint coordinates achieve equality in both signs. At p=1 the triangle inequality A,B<=kappa+tau and the same disjoint pair is sharp. For p=infinity the triangle inequality gives kappa+tau and x=e_i+e_j,y=e_i-e_j achieves it for both signs. At p=2 the formula matches 2^(-1/p)((kappa+tau)^p+|kappa-tau|^p)^(1/p). Quantification requires only two coordinates, arbitrary positive parameters and real standard ell_p; no finite sampling extrapolation.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns a specific sqrt(product) invariant, not the adjacent min-type or arithmetic-mean constants.
